# dith (JavaScript library)

> Deterministic dithering in WebAssembly for browsers, Node >= 20.16, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare Workers. One call, `dither(input, options)`, gives the same pixels and the same PNG bytes as the `dith` CLI with the same flags. ESM only, zero dependencies, fully typed.

## Use

```js
import { dither, generate, recipe, presets, palettes, algorithms, generators, init, DithError } from "dith";

const out = await dither(input, { preset: "manga" });       // or dither(input, "manga")
out.width; out.height; out.data;                            // RGBA Uint8ClampedArray
out.palette; out.histogram; out.source; out.working;        // hex colors, color usage, sizes
out.recipe;                                                 // complete recipe: replay with { recipe } or dith apply --recipe
out.toPNG(); out.toGIF();                                   // Uint8Array, byte-identical to the CLI
out.toSVG({ svgShape: "circle" });                          // string
out.toImageData(); out.toBlob("png"); out.toDataURL("png"); // png | gif | svg
out.encode("png");                                          // any format init() lists

const orb = await generate("sphere", { preset: "risograph", canvasWidth: 800, canvasHeight: 600 });
const full = await recipe({ preset: "gameboy", pixelSize: 3 });  // like --emit-recipe, renders nothing
const info = await init();  // optional: { version, formats, decoders }; init({ wasm: url | bytes }) or init({ decoders: true })
```

All functions are async. Results are synchronous objects.

## Inputs

- Pixels: `ImageData`, `{ data, width, height }` (RGBA, 4 bytes per pixel), or a previous result.
- Encoded PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP: `Uint8Array`, `ArrayBuffer`, any `ArrayBufferView`, `Blob`, `File`, `Response`.
- A string or `URL`: http(s), data: and blob: URLs are fetched. On Node, Bun and Deno a plain string is a file path (relative to the working directory) and `file:` URLs are read.
- Browsers only: `HTMLImageElement`, `HTMLCanvasElement`, `HTMLVideoElement`, `ImageBitmap`, `OffscreenCanvas`, `VideoFrame`.

## Options

`options` is a preset name or an object of the CLI flags in camelCase (`--pixel-size` is `pixelSize`, `--no-serpentine` is `serpentine: false`). Layering is the CLI's: `recipe` (object or JSON text), then `preset` (replaces the recipe), then every other option. Palette precedence: `colors` > `autoPalette` > `palette`. Colors are hex strings (`"#111"`, `"#f5efe6"`), as a comma-separated string or an array. An unknown option name is an error that lists the valid names.

<!-- options:start -->
| Option | Type | CLI flag | Recipe field | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | `Preset` | `--preset` |  |  |  |
| `recipe` | `Recipe \| string` | `--recipe` |  |  |  |
| `algorithm` | `Algorithm` | `--algorithm` | `dither.algorithm` |  | `"floyd-steinberg"` |
| `palette` | `Palette` | `--palette` | `palette` |  | `"bw"` |
| `colors` | `string \| string[]` | `--colors` | `palette` |  |  |

## Catalogs

Ask the library instead of guessing: `presets()` (id, name, description, tags, algorithm, recipe), `palettes()` (id, colors, ...), `algorithms()` (id, category, best_for, temporally_stable, ...), `generators()` (id, best_for, motion). The TypeScript types `Preset`, `Palette`, `Algorithm` and `Generator` are the same lists as string unions.

## Errors

Every failure throws `DithError` (`instanceof DithError`): `code`, `message`, `suggestion`, `validValues?`. `err.toJSON()` returns the CLI's envelope `{ status: "error", code, message, suggestion, valid_values? }`. Codes: `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (out-of-range value with the range in the message, unknown option, unknown choice, unreadable input, init options after loading), `UNKNOWN_PRESET`, `UNKNOWN_PALETTE`, `INVALID_HEX_COLOR`, `PALETTE_TOO_FEW_COLORS`, `INVALID_RECIPE_JSON`, `RUNTIME_ERROR` (corrupt image data). Fix the option named in the message and retry; `validValues` lists the accepted values when the set is finite.

## Runtimes and loading

- Browsers load `dith.wasm` (266 KB brotli) and decode encoded images with the browser. Browser JPEG decoding and canvas alpha differ slightly from the CLI's; `await init({ decoders: true })` before the first call loads `dith-decode.wasm` (381 KB brotli) for CLI-identical decoding. Opaque PNG, GIF and WebP are identical either way.
- Node, Bun, Deno and Workers load `dith-decode.wasm`, which decodes PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP. Other formats fail with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`: decode them yourself and pass pixels.
- Cloudflare Workers: the package's `workerd` export condition imports the .wasm as a module; nothing to configure.
- Bundlers: Vite (and webpack 5, untested) find the .wasm through `new URL(..., import.meta.url)`. Otherwise serve `dith/dith.wasm` yourself and call `init({ wasm: "/path/dith.wasm" })`.
- Deno needs `--allow-read` to load the .wasm and local files.

## Rules of thumb

- Render at the final size (`maxDim`, or `width` + `height` + `fit`); never scale a dithered image afterwards.
- Start from a preset, then override: `{ preset: "risograph", contrast: 0.2 }`. For print looks add `inkBelow: 0.2`, `paperAbove: 0.9`, `inkLines: 0.5`.
- Same input and options give the same bytes, everywhere. Keep `seed` fixed for reproducibility; change it for variations.
- Save `result.recipe` as JSON to reuse a look here or in the CLI (`dith apply in.png --recipe look.json -o out.png`).
- PNG is the right output almost always. Keep SVG output small (`maxDim` 120 to 320).
